title: Assuring
description: Showing that STEGO meets the bar it claims to meet. Lathe says which obligations have a test; Assuring shows that each automated test ran and passed at an exact commit, as a proof run the CI provider's trusted signer attests with the commit as its subject, never as a file committed back. Two gates read that evidence and the spec's coverage: a change may not lower the designed, built or proved share of the base branch, and a release needs every share at 100% with every proof passed at its commit. Anyone can read what a commit proved from the attestations alone.

title: Building
description: Turning a service's generated source into an artifact that anyone can rebuild and check: resolving its modules, a module cache recorded by digest that builds use with the network off, a build with the Go SDK its archetype pins that gives the same bytes every time, a build record that names every input, an image that holds only that build's executable on a scratch base with SPDX and CycloneDX SBOMs, a signature by its CI provider's trusted signer, and the checks that tie an executable, a source snapshot or an image back to its record.

title: Declaring
description: A service author or an agent states what one service is: its archetype, entities, collections, operations, component settings and slot bindings. The declaration is the only thing an agent writes. STEGO refuses an invalid declaration before it writes any file, in one strict input stage and one semantic stage, so a bad declaration cannot reach the output.

title: Distributing
description: Getting a fix to the services that already exist. STEGO can name every service that was built from a given component and version, it tells a consumer when what that consumer was built from is superseded or withdrawn, and it lets a component fix reach a service without a new compiler release. The compiler itself is qualified, signed and installed on a stated platform.

title: Delivering
description: The contract between a service and the platform it runs on. STEGO owns everything derivable from service.yaml, and the platform owns everything derivable from the environment. Delivering covers the thin CI pipeline (a GitHub Actions call to the platform's pinned reusable workflow, or the Konflux standard pipeline) with every STEGO check, the plain kustomize base, the Argo CD delivery object, the typed platform-requirements.yaml every service writes, and the check that an environment file supplies every requirement. Cluster, network and database infrastructure, replicas, disruption budgets and every value that differs per environment stay with the platform.

title: Extending
description: A service author adds the service's own rules at typed extension points. A component declares a slot with its contract, and a fill implements that contract and carries its own tests. The compiler refuses a binding to a slot that no generator invokes, so a dead extension point cannot ship.

title: Generating
description: Turning a declaration and a pinned registry into code. The same declaration and the same registry always produce the same code, and a repeated run changes nothing. Generation is the only way generated code changes: a hand edit shows as drift, and a fix arrives as a version bump and a new run, so every change is a diff a reviewer can read. An interrupted run recovers to a known state.

title: Supplying
description: A platform engineer writes the parts that every service shares: archetypes, components and mixins, with their config schemas, ports, slots and output contracts. Each component owns the contract for the code it emits. A common registry is trusted, and a local registry may add to it but never replace a part of it. A component carries a maturity stage, so a golden path never includes an experiment.
